Commentary.Commentary: We are back for the chase. The umpires are on the field and the fielders have taken their position on the field after discussing last-minute plans. David Warner and Travis Head will open the batting innings. Spin is introduced at the beginning as Mujeeb Ur Rahman will have the new ball in hand. Let the chase begin...
... THE RUN CHASE ...

Australia, on the other hand, grappled with the challenge of breaking the Afghan partnership in the middle overs, allowing Afghanistan to dominate the closing stages. Adam Zampa, who has been in formidable form for the Australians, could only secure a solitary wicket during this phase, thwarting their game plan. While Mitchell Starc, Pat Cummins, and Josh Hazlewood maintained their precision, the Afghan batters denied them any opportunity to regain control. Josh Hazlewood claimed two wickets, with Glenn Maxwell, Mitchell Starc, and Adam Zampa each chipping in with one wicket. The focus now shifts to Australia's innings under the lights as they set out to chase down the formidable target posted by Afghanistan. The stage is set for an enthralling showdown, as cricket enthusiasts eagerly anticipate whether Australia can clinch victory or if Afghanistan will once again defy expectations and secure a spot in the coveted top four of the tournament standings. The live-action awaits, and the answer will soon be revealed.

Ibrahim Zadran, the first-ever centurion for Afghanistan in World Cups is up for a chat. He says that he is very happy to achieve this special feat. Adds that against Pakistan, he missed out on his hundred and was desperately looking to score and he also had chats with his coaches and felt that there was a century around the corner. Tells that the ball is coming nicely on the bat and there target was something around 290 but if they had wickets in hand then they would have looked for 330. Praises Rashid Khan for his blinder of a knock in the end. Says that they have a good bowling attack but they need to execute their plans and bowl well. Mentions that the runs are on the board, half the job is done and now they have to field well. Ends by saying that he had a good chat with Sachin Tendulkar and is very thankful to him for sharing his experience and which also helped him score the hundred in this game.

The Afghan innings began on a promising note, with both openers displaying excellent form. The early loss of Rahmanullah Gurbaz's wicket in the eighth over, however, shifted the onus onto Ibrahim Zadran and Rahmat Shah to stabilize the innings. Together, they crafted a vital partnership of 83 runs, providing Afghanistan with a solid foundation. Rahmat Shah's departure marked a crucial moment in the innings, making way for Afghan skipper Hashmatullah Shahidi to partner with Ibrahim Zadran. The duo managed to amass an additional 50 runs before Hashmatullah Shahidi succumbed to an impeccable yorker delivered by Mitchell Starc. Ibrahim Zadran then went on to score an exceptional century which became the highlight of the innings, rendering him the first Afghan batter to register a World Cup ton. In the final overs, Ibrahim Zadran, alongside the dynamic Rashid Khan, accelerated the scoring, dispatching the Australian bowlers for colossal sixes and contributing 58 valuable runs in the last five overs of the innings. Ibrahim Zadran went not out at 129 and Rashid Khan scored a brilliant 35 off just 18 balls to take Afghanistan to 291.

The culmination of the first innings in this thrilling encounter between Australia and Afghanistan has set the stage for a riveting contest. Afghanistan's captain won the toss and opted to make first use of a pristine batting track at the illustrious Wankhede Stadium in Mumbai. The Afghan side delivered a stellar batting performance, accumulating an imposing total of 291 while losing just five wickets throughout their allocated 50 overs, ultimately setting the Australians a challenging target of 292 to chase. This remarkable feat now stands as Afghanistan's highest-ever World Cup score, marking a historic moment for their cricketing journey.

Commentary.Commentary: Done with the pre-match formalities! We can see the Australian players spread out and take their respective field positions. Rahmanullah Gurbaz and Ibrahim Zadran are the two openers for Afghanistan. Mitchell Starc has the new ball in hand and is raring to go. Let's play...

We are moments away from the game but before that, players from both sides make their way out in the middle and line up for their respective national anthems. It will be Afghanistan's first followed by the national anthem of Australia.

Pat Cummins, the captain of Australia says they would have batted first as well. Adds that he is really happy with the team winning five in a row and they have used 14 players and every player has contributed well. Tells that the weather will play a part as it is much cooler and the decision to go with an extra batter in their squad don't affect them much as they have plenty of bowling options. Informs Cameron Green and Steven Smith missed out while Mitchell Marsh and Glenn Maxwell make their way back in the team.

Hashmatullah Shahidi, the skipper of Afghanistan says they want to bat first as the wicket looks good for batting and they would like to put runs on the board. He adds by saying that the decision has been made keeping every aspect in mind along with the ground conditions up in hand. He extended his happiness of meeting the great Sachin Tendulkar before the start of the game and mentioned that he had a lot of points to share with the team. In the end, informs that they have one change in the team as Naveen-ul-Haq comes in for Fazalhaq Farooqi.

Australia (Playing XI) - Travis Head, David Warner, Mitchell Marsh (In place of Steven Smith), Marnus Labuschagne, Josh Inglis (WK), Glenn Maxwell (In place of Cameron Green), Marcus Stoinis, Pat Cummins (C), Mitchell Starc, Adam Zampa, Josh Hazlewood.

Afghanistan (Playing XI) - Rahmanullah Gurbaz, Ibrahim Zadran, Rahmat Shah, Hashmatullah Shahidi (C), Ikram Alikhil (WK), Azmatullah Omarzai, Mohammad Nabi, Rashid Khan, Mujeeb Ur Rahman, Noor Ahmad, Naveen-ul-Haq (In place of Fazalhaq Farooqi).
TOSS - Afghanistan have won the toss and they have elected to BAT first.

UPDATE - Steven Smith experienced some symptoms of vertigo last night which has troubled him before, and he also didn't look quite right in the practice sessions just before the match. This is another blow for the Aussies as Smith is doubtful for this game.

Afghanistan, on the other hand, have played some exceptional cricket in this World Cup and they have proved a lot of people wrong with their courage and determination. Their batting has been excellent with Rahmanullah Gurbaz and Ibrahim Zadran being very dependable openers and scoring a lot of runs while Rahmat Shah has scored three fifties on the bounce and will look to continue his form and captain Hashmatullah Shahidi has also played some decent knocks. Their middle order haven't been tested that much but whenever they have been, they have struggled a bit and that is an area they will look to improve. Their bowling has been really good with three world-class spinners Rashid Khan, Mohammad Nabi and Mujeeb Ur Rahman while the pacers Naveen-ul-Haq, Azmatullah Omarzai, and Fazalhaq Farooqi has supported them well too. They are riding high on confidence but this will be a really tough challenge and if they manage to get over the line here, it will be the best moment in their cricket history. Will they be able to do the unthinkable? Or will the Aussies prove to be too hard for them? We will find out soon. Toss and team news in a bit.

Australia have recovered brilliantly after a shaky start to this World Cup. David Warner and Mitchell Marsh had been giving them the good starts but the latter missed the last game due to personal reasons while Glenn Maxwell also did not play due to a minor injury and it will be interesting to see whether they come back or not. However, the return of Travis Head has been very effective for them while their middle order also got runs in the last game. Mitchell Starc, Josh Hazlewood, and Adam Zampa all have made important contributions with the ball and skipper Pat Cummins will hope that everything falls in place again and they get the all important victory.
